settings.name_in_paper: Budgeted causal MAB, cumulative regret, general graphs with hidden confounders
unmapped: arms are 2N+1 atomic interventions do(X_i=x) on binary variables plus observation a_0 in a known causal ADMG with hidden confounders
after each pull the learner observes all non-intervened variables of the causal graph (side information)

all interventional distributions P_x(y) are identifiable
budget-limited horizon: play until total cost exhausts budget B
settings.definition_quote: We study a causal MAB problem, in which a learner with a budget $B\geq0$ aims to minimize either its simple regret or cumulative regret. It is assumed that the learner knows the underlying causal graph.

settings.name_in_paper: Budgeted causal MAB, simple regret, general graphs
unmapped: arms are atomic interventions do(X_i=x) plus observation a_0 in a known causal ADMG with hidden confounders
after each pull the learner observes all non-intervened variables of the causal graph
the learner knows the causal graph and the non-uniform arm costs
settings.definition_quote: The simple regret of a learner using budget $B$ is defined by $R_{s}(B):= \mu_{a^*}- \mu_{\Tilde{a}_B}$, where $\Tilde{a}_B$ denotes the arm selected by the learner after exhausting budget $B$.

settings.name_in_paper: Budgeted causal MAB, cumulative regret (lower bound)
unmapped: arms are interventions do(X_i=x) on N variables each with domain size K_dom plus observation a_0 (N*K_dom+1 arms)
costs in [1, c_max]; the learner knows the causal graph and costs
settings.definition_quote: where $R_c(A_B,\mathcal{G}_N,P,\mathcal{C})$ denotes the cumulative regret of an adaptive algorithm $A_B$ with total budget $B$ on a causal graph $\mathcal{G}_N$ with $N$ nodes each of which has domain $\{1,...,K\}$. The reward distribution is $P$ and the set of costs is given by $\mathcal{C}=\{1\leq c_a\leq c| a\in\mathcal{A}\}$.

symbols.delta_0: cost-normalized gap of the observational arm: mu_{a*}/c_{a*} - mu_0
symbols.delta_ix: cost-normalized gap of arm a_{i,x}: mu_{a*}/c_{a*} - mu_{i,x}/c_{i,x}
symbols.p_ix: minimum probability over partitions/realizations of the conditioning events relevant to arm a_{i,x}
symbols.tau_ix: max{0, 1 - |V| W_i b_ix^{-p_ix^2/(2|V|)}}, W_i alphabet size of V\{X_i,Y}

conditions: all intervenable variables have identifiable causal effects P_{x_i}(y)
number of rounds T_B large enough to satisfy Lemma 16 (T >= max{e^{32/delta_0}, ...}) (used in the proof)
a* != a_0 (used in the proof, delta_0 > 0)
tuning: beta updated as min{2 sqrt(2)/(hat mu_tilde a/c - hat mu_0), sqrt(log t)}

source.label: th: cumu
source.quote: The expected cumulative regret of Algorithm \ref{alg: g-cumulative} is bounded by \delta_0 ( \frac{8\ln B}{\delta_{0}^2}+1 +\frac{\pi^2}{3} ) + \sum_{\delta_{i,x}>0}\delta_{i,x} (\frac{8\ln B}{\delta_{i,x}^2}+2 -\frac{8 p_{i,x}}{18\delta_0^2|\mathbf{V}|}\ln b_{i,x} \cdot \tau_{i,x,b} + \frac{\pi^2}{3} ), where b_{i,x} := \frac{8}{\delta_{i,x}^2} \ln (\frac{B}{\max_{a}c_a})+1, \tau_{i,x,b} :=...

results.notes: Regret is defined via expected rewards (means) relative to an optimum learner with budget B; comparator best_policy is approximate. Gaps are cost-normalized. Proof requires additional largeness conditions from Lemma 16 not stated in theorem.

symbols.n_q: cost-weighted infrequent-arm threshold n(q) = min{tau : sum_{i,x} c_{i,x} 1{q_{i,x} < tau^{-1/k_i}} <= tau}

conditions: all intervenable variables have identifiable causal effects
B >= max{B_1, B_2} (constants defined in proof)

source.label: th: simple g
source.quote: The expected simple regret of Algorithm \ref{alg: g-simple} is bounded by $\small{\mathcal{O}\Big(\sqrt{\frac{n(\mathbf{q})}{B} \log \frac{NB}{n(\mathbf{q})}}\Big)}$.

results.notes: Hidden constant M' depends on graph (c-component sizes). Setting c_{i,x}=1 recovers Maiti et al. bound (Remark 4).

symbols.n_qnew: n(q) computed with q_{i,x} = P(X_i = x); satisfies n(q_new) <= n(q)

conditions: no-backdoor causal graph (no unblocked backdoor paths from intervenable variables to Y)
tuning: hat q_{i,x} redefined as (2/B) sum_t 1{x_i^t = x}

source.label: remark: no
source.quote: Following the same procedure as in the proof of Theorem \ref{th: simple g}, it is straightforward to show that Algorithm \ref{alg: g-simple}, using $q_{i,x}^{new}$ and $\hat{q}_{i,x}^{new}$, achieves $R_s(B) \in \mathcal{O}\Big(\sqrt{\frac{n(\mathbf{q}^{new})}{B} \log \frac{NB}{n(\mathbf{q}^{new})}}\Big)$.

results.notes: Stated in the proof of a remark rather than a theorem; paper also shows n(q) <= c m'(q) when costs uniform c, improving on Nair et al.

symbols.c_max: upper bound c on arm costs (costs in [1, c])

conditions: max over causal graphs with N nodes, reward distributions and cost sets with 1 <= c_a <= c
hard instance: parallel graph with uniform costs c, rewards from a parametric family with twice-differentiable densities (e.g. unit-variance Gaussian)

source.label: sec:lower-cum
source.quote: We prove $\min_{A_B}\max_{\mathcal{C},\mathcal{G}_N,P'} R_c(A_B,\mathcal{G}_N,P,\mathcal{C})\geq \Omega\big(\sqrt{\lfloor B/c\rfloor KN}\big)$ in appendix \ref{sec:lower-cum}

results.notes: Explicit constant in appendix: floor(B/c)/(8e) * sqrt(KN/(w floor(B/c))) with w depending on Fisher information. Not a numbered theorem.
